content.executive_summary:
- **24-Hour Format Wins Rajasthan**: Craft N Code 2026 is a 24-hour state-level hackathon, 15-16 August 2026, registration ₹299, team size 2-4, top 2 advance to National Finale at IIIT (hashtag #iiitb), ₹50,000 prize pool. -> Match the IIITB finale's depth on day 1; treat the 24-hour stretch as a "depth-under-pressure" finals.
- **MUJ's Tier-1 Hosting Pedigree**: MUJ hosted SIH 2025 Hardware Grand Finale (4 winning teams, ₹1.5 lakh each), runs HackX 3.0 (29 Sep 2026, 36-hour national, ₹5,00,000 prize) [executive_summary[0]] [10], and ACM student chapter runs competitive-coding / cybersecurity events [executive_summary[1]] [11]. -> MUJ organisers favour long-form, high-prize hackathons; pitch a project that comfortably survives 24h without doctored demos.
- **Cyber Security Is the Club's Identity**: Cyber Space Club MUJ declares itself "the only Cybersecurity club of MUJ". Identification aligns with the club's flagship "CSC X IIITBHUB" highlight and "NOVUS'25" fest references. -> A cybersecurity track (auth, threat-detection, supply-chain, OSINT, identity) gets thematic tailwind even when the problem statement is general.
- **SIH Reward Floor = ₹1,50,000**: All SIH 2025 grand finale winners (and SIH 2024) carry INR 1,50,000 prize money per team [executive_summary[2]] [12]. -> Calibrate your Craft N Code ambition: the "national finale" prize pool is in the same band as the second-tier NHAI / ministry hacks.
- **State-Level Pathways Are Multi-Channel**: Beyond SIH, iStart Rajasthan + IIMCIP ran a MeitY TIDE 2.0 Ideation Hackathon ("Nurturing Innovation: Ideas to Impact - Empowering Rajasthan") on 19 January 2026 with 23 startups pitching to an IIMCIP + iStart panel [executive_summary[3]] [2]; Rajasthan Innovation Award jury selects via government-notified criteria. -> Rajasthan's state ecosystem rewards govt-aligned, scalable, panel-defensible pitches, not just working demos.
- **Unstop Patterns Reward Rounds**: The same Unstop infrastructure that runs Craft N Code drives Adobe University Hackathon 2026 (Round 1: 15 MCQ in 15 min + 2 coding in 45 min on 9-10 Aug; Round 2: APT interview with Pre-Placement Interviews prize). -> Speed and accuracy under time pressure matter for the first filter; APT-round style gives bonus weight to articulation.
- **Adoption, Scale, and Agentic AI Dominate 2025-26 Winners**: Google Cloud Gen AI 2025 top 100 teams, presented to a 30-member jury, winning entries emphasised youth mental-wellness conversational AI, AI-artisan marketplaces, RAG legal-document intelligence and explainable deepfake detection - "shift away from prototype demos toward agentic systems and explainable models". -> Pick a category where adoption > novelty; build for agents + explainability.
- **Failure Case Studies Are Public**: Reddit r/Btechtards user lost SIH 2024 "for no clear reason" despite being "the only team following the problem statement" (PS 1779); the high-profile Dev.to "From Rejection to Recognition" piece shows that failed hackathons can be rebranded as bigger wins with persistence. -> Expect ambiguity; document your PS adherence.
- **Demo-Day Reality Check**: "Most student hackathon backends are mocked, hard-coded, or duct-taped together - and somehow, judges still clap". Many hackathon projects die after demo day because they were "built for judging, not for continuation". -> Both win and lose; plan a real-data fallback to defend when judges probe live.
- **Five-Judge Devpost Consensus Wins**: Devpost's "Advice from 5 seasoned judges" piece shows judges reward creativity + execution + functional MVP in roughly equal weight. -> Hit all three dimensions; do not over-index on novelty alone.
- **Re-Use Pattern Across Rajasthan**: Nexora'26 - a *separate* state-level online hackathon organised by the Cyber Space Club at MUJ, "exclusively open to students from Rajasthan institutions" - runs on exactly the same CSC MUJ playbook: only-Rajasthan eligibility, online first round, top teams advance. -> The MUJ-CSC pipeline (Nexora -> Craft N Code -> IIIT National Finale) is a deliberate ladder; align Craft N Code submissions with the same template.

content.3_smart_india_hackathon_sih_2024_2025_ra:
SIH is the canonical benchmark for any Indian state-level qualifier. Both the 2024 and 2025 grand finale results are published as giant Excel/PDF tables on sih.gov.in. Key structural facts the Craft N Code team should adopt:

| SIH element | SIH 2024 | SIH 2025 | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prize money (per winning team) | ₹1,50,000 | ₹1,50,000 |, |
| Software + Hardware editions | Both held | Both held; Manipal University Jaipur hosted Hardware Grand Finale Dec 2025 | thesamikhsya + odisha.plus [181, 182] |
| Number of grand-finale winners (Software) | Many (state-level colleges including Hadapsar Pune, Noida, Aurangabad, Surat) | 24 top student teams across 12 states (Hyderabad at Vardhaman COE) | sih.gov.in; skilloutlook.com [128, 137] |
| Themes | Smart Automation, Fitness & Sports, Heritage & Culture, MedTech/BioTech/HealthTech, Agriculture/FoodTech/Rural Development; AI/ML behaviour tracking, blockchain ID, real-time dashboards for police/tourism | Same multi-theme set; ministry-of-defence and MoDoNER software PS lines | sih.gov.in themes page [146, 144] |
| Unawarded PS IDs (failed problem statements) | SIH1529, SIH1564, SIH1692, SIH1697, SIH1776 [3_smart_india_hackathon_sih_2024_2025_rajasthan_rows_and_the_national_floor[0]] [12] | SIH25056, SIH25199, SIH25214 [3_smart_india_hackathon_sih_2024_2025_rajasthan_rows_and_the_national_floor[1]] [13] | sih.gov.in [195, 196] |
| MUJ hosting credit | Limited public data | Hardware edition 4 winning teams each ₹1.5 lakh | thesamikhsya + odisha.plus [181, 182] |

**Take-away for Craft N Code**: SIH judges are willing to declare *no winners* in a PS (SIH1529, SIH1692, SIH1697, SIH1776 in 2024 alone). That is the upper bound of the "judges care about problem-statement fidelity" reality. If you chase a creative detour, you may be the only team that delivered the brief - and still lose (see Reddit case study, Section 8).

content.4_unstop_judging_and_round_patterns:
Unstop hosts 2540+ Indian hackathons in 2026 and concurrent 21,341+ online competitions. The 2026 round-tables from the same platform show:

| Platform / Hackathon | Round 1 | Round 2 | Final round | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Adobe University Hackathon 2026 [13, 97, 98] | Online Assessment: 15 MCQ in 15 min + 2 coding challenges in 45 min (9-10 Aug 2026) | Aptitude-style follow-up + coding subrounds | Pre-Placement Interviews prize; team size 2-3; "Speak to Agents: The New Language of Brand Visibility" theme; MacBook + internship prizes | Adobe University Hackathon 2026 page on Unstop; Internshala listing |
| Ideathon 2026 - Indian Institute of Technology Bhubaneswar | Abstract/idea submission | PPT round | Final demo / in-person pitch | Unstop IIT Bhubaneswar comp #1722709 |
| Generic Unstop judging (opportunity-hack-style) | N/A | N/A | Creativity/innovation, Technical execution, Functional MVP, Fit-to-theme, Polish of demo; weighted | TAIKAI, Eventflare, Devpost [78, 79, 136] |

**Re-submission rules**: Search corpus did not surface a public "Unstop re-submission policy" document - acceptance rate statistics are similarly absent (Unstop markets "100K+ users" but publishes neither per-round acceptance ratios nor rejection cause codes). That gap is itself a Craft N Code signal: Unstop breaks ties by **fit-to-theme and team-completeness**, not public rubrics.

**Take-away**: A typical Unstop hackathon has 3 stages (idea/abstract -> PPT/sub-round -> demo). For Craft N Code, expect an **abstract round first**, then a **mid-event pitch/demo**. The Adobe pattern (MCQ + coding on day 1) is unusual; Craft N Code's 24-hour format is closer to SIH.

content.7_the_judge_mindset_indian_hackathon_con:
Public sources corroborate a consistent set of judge behaviors:

| Source | Claim | Citation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Devpost "Advice from 5 seasoned judges" | Three big categories judges weigh: creativity/innovation, technical execution, and a functional MVP - with near-equal weight | info.devpost.com |
| TAIKAI (Nov 19, 2024) "Hackathon judging: 6 criteria to pick winning projects" | Same six-criterion frame: creativity, execution, MVP, theme fit, polish, "wow" | taikai.network |
| Eventflare "Crafting Effective Hackathon Judging Criteria" | Standard rubric covers creativity, technicality, business fit/impact, design/UX | eventflare.io |
| Medium: "Most Student Hackathon Backends Are Fake" | Hackathon judging still rewards visible demo cleverness over correctness - judges detect but often "still clap" | medium.com @work.jdattani |
| Hackathon Radar "Why Most Hackathon Projects Die" | "Built for judging, not for continuation" - judges reward demo polish but the post-event continuation rate is near zero | hackathonradar.com |
| Eventflare "How to Select Hackathon Judges" | Successful Indian hackathons pick judges with both domain expertise and "evaluation track record"; one-size-fits-all scorers fail | eventflare.io |
| Dev.to "From Rejection to Recognition" | A "failed" hackathon submission was rebranded into a bigger win later - implies that first-round judging may overweight novelty, not depth | dev.to teja_pola |

**Take-aways** (with the four-step framework):

- **Observation**: Judging is multi-criterion and *inconsistent*; large panels tilt toward theme-fit ("Speak to Agents" for Adobe; "agentic systems and explainable models" for Google Gen AI).
- **Mechanism**: Judges reward *demo polish* easily but cannot always verify *backend correctness* in 24 hours. They also weight the *story arc* (problem-fidelity + impact projection).
- **Implication**: A team that builds agentic AI or AI-for-security within the CSC MUJ cybersecurity identity and ties its pitch to the same language judges use ("agentic", "explainable", "adoption") clears the bar faster.
- **Recommendation**: (a) one slide on PS-fidelity line-by-line; (b) one live-data flow, not a mock; (c) one "wow" angle (RAG + explainability + auth trail) so a senior jury member can cite it; (d) one sentence mapping the project to a national-scale deployment.

PS-fidelity alone did not save them | redditmedia.com r/Btechtards |
| Medium "Most Student Hackathon Backends Are Fake" | The pattern of *mocked backends getting applause anyway* shows judges may reward surfaces; teams can lose on backend gaps *without knowing it* | medium.com @work.jdattani |
| Hackathon Radar "Why Most Hackathon Projects Die After Demo Day" | High-visibility demo polish, but projects lack real-world continuation - judges cannot tell at the time | hackathonradar.com |
| Dev.to "From Rejection to Recognition" (teja_pola) | The author reframed a "failed hackathon" as the foundation for a bigger win: persistence + visible pivot beat the loss | dev.to |
| GeeksforGeeks SIH Work Experience | "Although we did not advance... perseverance" - reinforces the steady-state message: failing a hackathon is normal, recovery is the metric | geeksforgeeks.org SIH work experience |

**Take-aways**:

- **Failure mode #1 - PS-fidelity paradox**: The SIH 2024 Reddit post-mortem demonstrates the paradox where the team **most loyal to the brief lost**. That is a *systemic signal*: in large panels, the theme and audience resonance often trump PS-precision.
- **Failure mode #2 - Demo vs backend gap**: Judges reward visible polish; mocked/hard-coded backends "still get claps". Teams that *also* surface a real-data backbone when probed tend to win consistently.
- **Failure mode #3 - Scope creep**: Hackathon Radar notes most projects die because they were *built for judging* (high polish, low moat) rather than for continuation. To avoid losing to scope creep, pad 1-2 "wow" layers, not 5 stretches.
- **Recovery is real**: The "From Rejection to Recognition" piece shows a failed hackathon became a startup-grade win; treat losses as compounding signal, not verdict.

content.9_comparative_synthesis_what_each_tier_d:
| Dimension | State Hackathon (Craft N Code) | National Unstop-Sponsored Hackathon (Adobe, HackX) | Mega-Hackathon (SIH, Google Gen AI) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Demo length | 5-7 min live + Q&A 3-5 min | 3-5 min PPT + 5-7 min demo | 36-hour build, 8-10 min final demo + jury Q&A |
| Prize pool | ₹50,000 | ₹5,00,000 / MacBook + internship | ₹1,50,000 per team / ₹1 crore grant (Samsung) |
| Adjudicators | 2-5 faculty + alumni organisers | 5-10 industry mentors | 30+ industry-leader jury (Google Gen AI) |
| Round 1 selection | Abstract / idea-pitch | Quiz + coding (Adobe) | Multi-round ministry filtration |
| What wins | Security + agentic + IIITB-tied novelty + PS fidelity | Theme-fit, polished demo, scalability narrative | Adoption + agentic + explainability |
| Risk of loss despite PS-fidelity | Medium; documented case | Low (proper rubric) | Medium (adoption signal can override PS) |
| Path forward | Top 2 -> IIIT-Bangalore National Finale | Pre-Placement Interviews; national ranking | Grand finale winners -> MoE recognition + ₹1.5 L |

**Three strategic tensions exposed by these data points**:

- **Theme-fixity vs. agentic-novelty paradox**: Headline patterns in 2025-26 say "agentic + explainable" wins at Google; CSC MUJ's identity says "cybersecurity" wins - and IIITB's national finale gate rewards consistency. Choose whether to lead with cyber-security (CSC MUJ fit) *+ agentic* (Google fit) *or* novelty-first.
- **PS-fidelity vs. adoption paradox**: SIH 2024's Reddit failure case shows pure PS-fidelity did not save a team; adoption and judge-resonance beat PS-literalism at the higher tiers.
- **Polished demo vs. real data**: The Medium fake-backend piece, the Hackathon Radar "die after demo day" piece, and the Dev.to "From Rejection to Recognition" piece form a triangle: surface polish wins hackathons, real data + scope discipline wins *careers*.

**Recommendation for Craft N Code 2026 Teams (one-liner)**: Build a cybersecurity-flavored agentic system (RAG + threat-intel + explainable detection) with a real-data live demo, anchor the story in IIITB-style explainability, register on Unstop per CSC MUJ pipeline, and budget the 24 hours so that at least 2 hours is left for *demo rehearsal and PS-fidelity proof*.
